Ptolemy and the scholars who are experts in the sphere of the zodiac say that the stars fixed upon the tail of the Dragon traverse the zodiacal signs, one degree per hundred solar years in the direction of the zodiac, such that the two great ones are approximately fifteen farsakhs apart, and one full revolution takes thirty-six thousand years. According to Khwaja Nasir al-Din Muhammad Tusi — may God have mercy on him — and a number of later scholars, for every seventy years there are two degrees, so that in twenty-four thousand and sixty years one full revolution is completed. According to Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi, Abu'l-Husayn al-Sufi, Abu Rayhan al-Biruni, and most later scholars, for every sixty-six solar years there is one degree, such that in twenty-three thousand and seven hundred years one revolution is completed. Abu Ma'shar Anzad al-Ri Kabzi, as he is called in the Kitab al-Uluf, agrees that the planets and the fixed stars return to the same degree and minute at the moment of their creation — and this is evidence that all conditions recur between those two periods. It is reported that it was at this time that the Flood occurred, and God knows best.

As for the ninth sphere, which is devoid of stars, it is called for this reason the Starless Sphere (Falak al-Atlas). All scholars have said that this name was given to it because it moves with such swiftness that all the other spheres are carried along within it and revolve by its motion. According to this view, it is called the Greatest Sphere (Falak al-A'zam) because of its great size, and it is also called the Supreme Sphere because of its extreme speed. A line drawn from its two stationary poles around the earth is called the equator (Khat al-Mu'tadal al-Nahar), and the rotation of this sphere continuously follows the path of that circle.

Below the line, from the two-layered sphere, it runs straight, and both celestial poles are on the horizon. As one moves toward the north by degrees, the northern pole rises, until when one arrives at the point where the northern pole is at the zenith, that southern sphere disappears. On the southern side of the equatorial line, if the world were tilted and there were no stillness, the same situation would apply, and the southern pole would rise until it reaches the zenith.

This is not unique to these shapes. Plato and others have said the same thing, and some have said that the spherical body moves in a circular motion, and they call the proof of this obvious. And Pythagoras said it is possible, and some have said that it has no center, and this is the correct position. Aristotle said it has neither body nor meaning, and it is impossible for it to move.

The true nature and essence of this matter is beyond the capacity of intellect to comprehend. Each great celestial sphere has stars within it, and there are several other spheres, each with its own name, such as the rotating spheres, the equant, the eccentric, the inclined sphere, the deferent, and the epicycle.

The cause of the sphere's revolution is straight and correct. The nodes where the spheres intersect are called the Head and Tail of the Dragon. The nodes of each sphere — the astronomers call the northern node the Head of the Dragon (Ra's al-Tinnin), and it is also called the ascending node. The southern node is called the Tail of the Dragon (Dhanab al-Tinnin), and in astronomical tables it is noted as the descending node.

Because the straight river, solar eclipses, and lunar eclipses are related to it, and Sunbur gave it the count of nine years and seven months, and they said a little less; and according to some opinions there is a slight variation more or less, and these nodes of it are the fortunate head, and Taro diminishes it and the two things of Zuhr stand opposite it, and the two are in the station of depression. This is an indicator of raids upon things, and the tail indicates conditions that are recorded accordingly.

And so Zuhra is a changing planet, and at the head of the sphere it leads the spheres of the seven planets and is deficient; it is in the highest of the spheres and slow in motion, and for this reason it is one hundred and something. And in this date that has passed — forty and seven hundred of the Hijra — it stood thus: Muhammad was born and his birth corresponds to the fourth of the month, in the year eighty-three, and al-Ghazali in the second month of the year six and thirty, and what belongs to al-Awzabi as it was settled; and the fourth month of the year sixty-one in the reckoning of Maliki, and the eighth month — Mihr-month — of the year eighty-seven in the Persian Yazdegerdi reckoning, and the ninth of Tammuz of the year one thousand and fifty-one in the Alexandrian Syriac reckoning.

According to Abu Rayhan and the Zij Khafi, the position of the dark planets requires, by the Zij Khani, calculated by the pen: by this reckoning the shadow of Venus in arc is seven degrees and some minutes; Zuhra according to Abu Rayhan is sixty-three degrees and fifty-three minutes, and by the Zij Khani eighty-four degrees and eight minutes. Jupiter by Abu Rayhan is four degrees, and by calculation it stands at sixty-three degrees and some minutes; by the Zij Khani it is ten degrees and five minutes, retrograde at thirty and four-tenths. Saturn is nine degrees and eight minutes; when it reaches Scorpio by Abu Rayhan it is seventeen degrees and seventeen minutes, and by the Zij Khani it is fifteen degrees and fifty minutes.

The two deputies of the Sun: that Cancer is at twenty-three degrees, twenty-some minutes, as stated in the Noble Book: "And the sun runs to its resting place — that is the decree of the All-Knowing." The ecliptic encompasses the sphere of the zodiac, and each degree it traverses produces changes through the inclination of the celestial sphere. Therefore, the head of Zuhra (Venus) by nature falls in Pisces at eleven degrees and fifteen minutes; according to Abu Rayhan, the head of Zuhra in Virgo is twenty-nine degrees and twenty-some minutes. The two deputies — the visible and the hidden node — at nineteen degrees and five minutes, making the connection at seventeen degrees and nineteen minutes. According to Abu Rayhan, the head of Zuhra in Capricorn is twenty-eight degrees and twenty-three minutes, and the hidden node of Dallul at two degrees and two minutes, and the two deputies of Qamar (Moon) at fifteen degrees and eight minutes. The head of Zuhra in Capricorn is twenty-nine degrees and twenty-four minutes. The lesser sphere is thus, because it is simple in itself; everything together does not increase nor diminish, and it is variable. The center of Kharf in that is not balanced, and the desired center is dry, cold, moist, male, feminine, diurnal, nocturnal, and so forth — this is well-known. Those who divide the zodiac into the aforesaid divisions: Virgo is the established reference, and it indicates the lower world in this sense. Each sphere has its particular place and a singular, immovable essence; it goes here and there, moves, advances, and retreats over a duration of time and place, opposite and touching one another over periods of time and place, also opposite in course. The celestial sphere proceeds rightly, and the count of three hundred and sixty degrees of the sphere — that is, the measure of the Sun's journey in a day and the duration of a day and night — according to the Indian reckoning is sixty karī, each karī being sixty parts, the measure of a sixtieth part being...

The just measure of a human breath: in the span of a day and night, one draws twenty-some thousand breaths. According to the opinion of some scholars, there are twenty-four hours in a day and night, each hour consisting of eight minutes, calculated on the basis that in each minute the measure of fifteen breaths is drawn by a person. According to the view of the majority, each hour is divided into forty parts, and in each part the measure of ten breaths is taken.

By means of the ninth sphere, the eight celestial orbs contained within it revolve in a direction opposite to their own proper motion, while the elemental sphere of earth remains stationary at the center. From east to west is the result of the motion of the encompassing spheres, and from west likewise, so that the orbs are bound therein. The seven celestial spheres move from east to west, and the motion of each in its course is contrary to the others — this is called the second motion, also termed the eastern motion. The motion of the eighth sphere, called the Sphere of the Zodiac, moves from west to east, and its poles...

The fourth [sphere] is the place of the Sun, and an explanation of the duration of its course is given here. The eight spheres mentioned above move in the order of the zodiacal signs, as they required. Thus the ninth sphere became necessary so that the light of the sun would fall upon one side of the earth, and just as it is described: the light falls upon one side and darkness falls upon the other side of the world. It does not increase or decrease, and upon the inhabited quarter of the earth's surface it alternates. This is what is meant by day and night, and the reckoning of week, month, and year is based on this calculation.

The opposition of the motions of the stars, and the precedence of day, is confirmed by the word of the Glorious Quran: "It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each floats in its own orbit" (Quran 36:40). This is the established usage among the scholars of Islam, and the reckoning of days is based upon it.

Now we calculate the years and months in order, following the proper method. In this chapter I will recall and record in it a portion of historical events.

The calendars used in this discourse are six in number, of Islamic origin. The Arab Islamic months and years are counted, and the result of the calculation is that each year has three hundred and sixty-five days, and its months are of varying lengths. According to the scholars, the calculation comes to three hundred and sixty-four days and a fraction — that is, eleven [additional fractions of days] — and the months are arranged accordingly in a proportional manner.

The names of the Islamic months are: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Akhir, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhira, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja. Of these months, four are sacred: Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, Muharram, and Rajab. The divine word informs us of their number: God Almighty said, "Verily, the number of months with God is twelve months in God's Book, from the day He created the heavens and the earth." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Time has returned to how it was the day God created the heavens and the earth." Of these, three are consecutive and one is solitary: the three consecutive ones are Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, and Muharram, and the solitary one is Rajab. It is reported in the hadith: "Rajab is the month of God, Sha'ban is my month, and Ramadan is the month of my community." The first rulings were established for the people accordingly. Most months have twenty-nine or thirty days. The Hijri calendar dates from the Prophet's migration from Mecca, and in this system the years of the Hijra are counted.

The fifth epistle concerns the revelation, and among the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan, the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) most likely falls on the twenty-seventh, as the majority of scholars agree. The mention of the word "it" (the Night) in Surah "Inna anzalnahu" (Surah al-Qadr) occurs three times, and the most appropriate proof from the word itself is that it falls on the twenty-seventh. The first of Shawwal is Eid al-Fitr. Fasting six days after Eid completes the fast, and this is highly recommended for the people.

On the twentieth of Dhu al-Qa'dah, pilgrims set out toward the Ka'bah, and Adam went there with the best of pilgrims. These are the Days of Dhu al-Hijjah, which are sacred months. On the eighth day, they proceed onward, and on the Day of Arafah they must be present at Arafat and perform the Hajj. The sacrifice of Eid al-Adha is performed as a thanksgiving for completing the Hajj. The eleventh, twelfth, and thirteenth are the Days of Tashriq, also called the Counted Days; fasting on these days is forbidden.

On the first of Dhu al-Hijjah, the Lord of Sovereignty and the Shah of Guardianship became brothers in faith. On the twenty-fourth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the Prophet engaged in Mubahala (spiritual contest) with the People of the Book and the Family of the Prophet, and on the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth are the White Days (Ayyam al-Bid).

Among the innovations that heretics have introduced is what some call "the first of Ramadan," attributed to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Abd Allah, marking the defeat of the followers of the Caliphs by Abu Hasan al-Husayn — though the common people wrongly attribute this to others.

On the eighteenth of Ramadan, certain heretics celebrate "Eid al-Qiyam," claiming to follow the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, peace be upon him. This is also counted among innovations. It is said that their festival commemorates when the Imam of the Age appeared anew from the time of the Prophet, peace be upon him, until now — which I have explained in another book in brief summary. This account begins from before his birth and carries forward to the time of Abd Allah.

Al-Muṭṭalib passed away, and his lineage was unbroken by anyone. It is said that from the time of the ancient Persians, no man had come like him, and he was a eunuch and fell ill in his youth, and eventually departed. The Prophet of God, peace be upon him, appeared as a light to the people, and the three leaders came forward. He also built palaces in Syria, and the people of Iskandaria and others were present in the Year of the Elephant. In the year of the reign of the just king Khusraw Anushirwan, it is confirmed by the scholars that it is correct: In the time of the just king Anushirwan, the Commander of the Faithful Ali, peace be upon him, was born, and in that same year his aunt's family was illuminated. The testimony is confirmed: the priest came with the message, and Wahb came and gave the message at eighteen years. At seven years of age, at the time of his return journey, Abu Aba passed away. His names were conveyed to Abd al-Muṭṭalib, and grace was given. In that same year, in the eighth year, the Abyssinians conveyed news to Abd al-Muṭṭalib, may God be pleased with him. He passed away, and Abu Ṭālib, his paternal uncle, brought him, and at twelve years the priest Jubayr gave the message of prophethood. At nineteen years, he set out on the hajj journey and gained experience. At twenty years, he went to the arbitration of the Black Stone and overcame the matter. He prevailed. At twenty-five years, Umar was born. At twenty-two years, he attained the status described, and gained great benefit.

And at the age of twenty-four, together with Maysara, the servant of Khadija bint Khuwaylid, he went on a trading journey, brought back great profit, met the monk Bahira on the road, and received the glad tidings of prophethood.

And at the age of twenty-five, he married Khadija bint Khuwaylid and lived with her for twenty-five years, and despite her presence he never desired another, and the wonder of his noble character endured for forty years. At the age of thirty, the Commander of the Faithful Ali, peace be upon him, was born inside the Kaaba — no other birth had occurred inside the Kaaba except for his. And at the age of thirty-five, it came about that they undertook the restoration of the Kaaba, and the governor entrusted the placement of the Black Stone by the blessed hand of Abu Dakyd to Ali; and 'Abd al-Zanat, son of the daughter of Abu al-'As ibn Abi 'Abd Manaf, was brought forward. At the age of forty he was honored with the nobility of revelation — that was in the forty-first year of the Era of the Elephant, the twenty-first year of the Alexander era,

and the nineteenth year of the reign of Khusraw Parviz. From the first of Rajab until Ramadan — a period of six months — the appearance of the religion and the command of prophethood came, along with signs, visions, greetings, and such like matters. And on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan, at the time of the morning meal in the cave of Hira, Gabriel, peace be upon him, appeared shining and the word of God was revealed — the very first of it being: "Read in the name of your Lord who created," — and the noble words certifying the obligation of the fast of Ramadan from that news: "The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed." And the heavenly books such as the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Scrolls were each likewise revealed in the month of Ramadan: the Scrolls on the first, two others on the sixth, the Gospel on the twelfth, and the Quran was sent down on the twenty-fourth. And in the month of Shawwal the Pleiades [rose],

and the Quraysh came to know of the message. And in the second year of revelation, Fatima bint Rasul Allah was born, and [the rest is partially illegible] the child of the Messenger, Salman.

Khadija came before the revelation, and from the lineage of al-Baynan, and in the third year of the call it was a general matter concerning the affairs of religion and Islam. The Commander of the Faithful Ali was appointed scribe, and [there were] four among them. The cursed Ubayy's hostility toward Mustafa began, and the oppressors of the unbelievers started, and the Prophet bound the Muslims [in covenant] and imposed [conditions] upon Quraysh, and the Prophet gave guarantees. The daughter of Anash and Ubayy ibn Abi Lahab divorced her so that the Prophet could [marry] Hafsa. The Prophet said: "O God, unleash upon him a dog from among Your dogs," and a lion tore him apart, and the Prophet gave Ruqayya in marriage to Uthman. In the fifth year of the revelation, in the month of Rajab, some gifts were given by command, and [Muslims] migrated to Abyssinia, and in the same year [the people of] Quraysh and Banu Hashim formed a pact, and for eight months they cut off dealings with al-Baynan and did not speak to them. In the sixth year of the revelation occurred the miracle of the splitting of the moon. In the tenth year and in the ninth year of the revelation, most of the Arab tribes became Muslim. In the tenth year of the revelation, in the month of Dhu al-Qa'da, Abu Talib died — the Prophet, peace be upon him, [mourned] three days — and [then] Khadija, the honored wife of the Prophet, died, and [this period] is called the Year of Grief. In the eleventh year, they gave Ghashiya [in marriage] and brought her as a bride but he did not take her with him, and Sawda bint Zam'a was brought to him and he took her with him. Then he went to Ta'if; the servants [spent] two months and two days there, and returned. On the way, some jinn had embraced Islam, and the surah "Say: It has been revealed to me" — that a group of jinn heard it — is a witness to this. The Prophet called on the tribes and clans. Adi ibn Ludhul ibn Ubayd of the Quraysh came to Mecca and [the Muslims were] besieged in the Shi'b. And in that same year, in the month of Rajab on the twentieth, [something] was established; the killing of five [persons] was decreed. In the twelfth year of the revelation, the people of Medina were called [to Islam], and in the thirteenth [year] the migration [Hijra] began.

It was from Mecca to Medina, and the beginning of the Hijri calendar dates from there; in the first month of Hijra, the individual came to perform jihad, which is obligatory, and prayers were arranged in this order as recorded, and from that time a fixed account was established. In Dhu al-Hijja of that year, he took Aisha with him, and that year he set out for the campaign against Quraysh. In the fourth year of the Hijra, there was discord between the Prophet's daughter Fatima and Ali, peace be upon him. There were the expeditions of Abu Tarad, Dhat al-Ushra, and Badr the First, and Batn al-Khayl; in the month of Sha'ban the fasting of Ramadan was commanded. The great battle took place, and forces came to the aid of the people of Islam, and Abu Jahl and the idols of Quraysh were slain, and in that same year occurred the death of Ruqayya, daughter of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). In Medina he conducted affairs, and the Messenger (peace be upon him) contracted the marriage of Umm al-Kulthum. The expedition against Banu Qaynuqa' and Suwayyiq took place, and in the month of Dhu al-Hijja of that year the sacrifice was ordained. The Battle of Dhu Qarad took place between the Arabs, and in that year the Arabs were gathered and were victorious, blessing the name of the Messenger whenever they mentioned him in battle. The Battle of Khaybar took place, and he commanded: "Seek guidance from the Arabs by means of the pilgrimage." In the third year of the Hijra there were expeditions; he gave the command and the leaders of the Jews were slain; the spoils were distributed. The birth of Amir al-Mu'minin Hasan ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, took place; in the month of Ramadan the Prophet's tooth was broken. In the month of Shawwal, the Battle of Uhud took place, in which the blessed face of the Messenger of God was struck and his blessed countenance was wounded, and the master of martyrs attained martyrdom. Also in the fourth year of the Hijra, the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin Husayn, peace be upon him, took place, and there were the expeditions to Najm, Sari', and Banu Nadir. The Prayer of Fear was performed. A marriage was arranged with Zaynab bint Khuzayma, and she was given in marriage.

He stayed with her for two months in the synagogue, and in the year five of the Hijra, in the month of Muharram, he took Zaynab bint [Jahsh] to himself in a marriage that God Almighty had arranged between them. In the middle of Rabi al-Awwal, the Expedition of Dhu al-Jayl took place, and in the month of Shawwal, the Battle of the Trench occurred, along with the combat of Ali al-Murtada and the slaying of Amr and Antar, and the scattering of Amr ibn Saud's troops — this is well known from the repelling of the disbelievers' army in that battle. In the month of Dhu al-Qadah, the Expedition against Banu Qurayza took place.

In year six of the Hijra, there were the Expeditions of Banu Lihyan and the raid on Banu al-Mustaliq, and the affair of Aisha and the revelation of the verses of her innocence. In the month of Ramadan, Juwayriyya bint al-Harith was taken in marriage. The truce with Quraysh at al-Hudaybiyya was concluded, and the Pledge of Ridwan was sworn. The deaths of kings who entered Islam occurred, and Negus, the king of Abyssinia, gave the daughter of Abu Sufyan in marriage; the Prophet accepted this marriage arrangement. In the same year, the Prophet prayed for rain, and when no rain fell, he said: "O God, water us all around and not upon us," and by this means rain ceased falling within the city of Medina but fell in the surrounding areas.

In year seven of the Hijra, in the month of Muharram, the conquest of Khaybar took place, and the heroic deeds of the Commander of the Faithful Ali in that battle are well known. The people of Fadak and Wadi al-Qura submitted. The Prophet turned away from Zahrat al-Hilal, and the expedition to al-Raji did not succeed. That same year, Safiyya bint Huyayy of Khaybar was brought to him in marriage, and Umm Kulthum, the daughter of the Messenger of God, departed. For the Messenger's mosque a pulpit was built, and he performed the compensatory Umra, and Maymuna bint al-Harith was taken in marriage.

In year eight of the Hijra, there were campaigns against the Arab tribes, and in Jumada al-Ula, the Expedition of Mu'ta in Syria took place. In the month of Ramadan, the conquest of Mecca occurred, followed by the Battle of Hunayn — the army also came to the aid of the Muslims at Hunayn. After that came the Expedition of Ta'if and campaigns against the Banu Fahr and various Arab tribes and Faran.

The Prophet, and the birth of Ibrahim, son of the Prophet, and the daughter of the Caliph Kalbi entering into marriage with the Prophet; she came and died soon after, and in the year six of the Hijra, the veiling of women from men was ordained. And the campaign of Butayla and the destruction of the mosque of the Quran, and the obligation of fighting upon Muslims was established. Mention is made of the marriage of certain women to the Prophet, and Fatima's son was set free. A child came into the Prophet's marriage, and his servant al-Madani was poisoned in this world, and the companions suffered greatly. They bore witness that the Prophet overcame the world, and in the year ten of the Hijra, the obligation of paying zakat was established. The believers' assembly was organized, and mention is made of the passing of Ibrahim, son of the Prophet, and the Farewell Pilgrimage. In the year eleven of the Hijra, the fitna of Musaylima the Liar, al-Aswad al-Ansi, and Tulayha al-Asadi appeared, each claiming prophethood falsely. In the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, the Prophet passed away, and the caliphate of Abu Bakr began. He was caliph for approximately two and a half years. It is related from the Prophet: the rightly-guided caliphs shall be thirty years. Abu Bakr sent Ibrahim ibn Ali and others to deal with the apostates. The cause of the Prophet's death is recounted: he was poisoned, and this incident took place at a certain gathering. In the month of Ramadan, Fatima, daughter of the Prophet, passed away. Ali, relying on the strength of Islam, marched with cavalry and infantry and brought many back to Islam. In the year eleven as well, the mission of Sajah, the prophetess of the Banu Tamim, arose, and she allied with Musaylima the Liar. The conquest of Yemen and the battle of Yamama, and the killing of Musaylima, are recorded here.

And the liberation, meaning Arab Iraq, was carried out by Khalid ibn al-Walid, who by the power of his devotion to Islam overcame and prevailed, and all harm was averted. In the thirteenth year of the Hijra, there was a campaign in Rome, and the conquest of some of the lands of Syria took place in Jumada al-Akhira. Abu Bakr sent forth and for years, months, and seven days this was the duration of the caliphate. And Abd al-Rahman, under whose authority Umar carried out the great conquest of Syria — and the halting at Khabar for Arab Iraq — occurred in the fourteenth year of the Hijra, approximately. And the liberation of the lands of Sawad, which are called the districts of the Quran, took place. In the fifteenth year of the Hijra came the conquest of all the lands of Syria, and in the sixteenth year the conquest of all of Arab Iraq was completed, and Yazdegerd ibn Shahraran was driven out and expelled, and that king entered under the protection and rule of Islam, and tribute and fixed tax were imposed upon those peoples. In the seventeenth year of the Hijra, there were grants and endowments from Bakr and Rabi'a. In the eighteenth year, Abu Ubayda al-Jarrah was present until the end of the year, and there was plague and pestilence. And the conquest of the province of Azerbaijan and Armenia — meaning the land of the Armenians — and some parts of Fars took place, along with a settlement and peace. In Syria, in the nineteenth year, and in the twentieth year the wives of the Prophet passed away among those women, and Sawda bint Rabi'a, also a wife of the Prophet, died. And the conquest of Egypt, Alexandria, Bahrain, and the province of Yemen took place. In the twenty-first year, the rich veins were discovered, and the provinces of Persian Iraq were conquered. In the twenty-second year, the conquest of all the Persian provinces was completed, as well as Qumish and the lands formerly under the Zoroastrians — namely Fars, Kerman, Sistan, and Khurasan — and Yazdegerd Shahraran was routed and fled to Khurasan, then to Ferghana and Turkestan. And in the twenty-third year, in the month of Dhu al-Hijja, he died.

Umar ibn al-Khattab held the caliphate for ten years, six months, and seven days. During his reign, the religion of Islam grew strong, gained ascendancy over all other religions, and spread far and wide. Through the power of Islam, he established himself in Medina, humbled the Caesar of Rome, and during a sermon said, "O mountain traveler, O Abu Zad," and the news reached Sariya so that he could take refuge. In the year twenty-four, Hafsa, daughter of Umar, passed away. In the year twenty-five, there were events concerning Mary and Noah, and campaigns against the peoples of Andalusia. In the year twenty-six, the armies of Islam triumphed over the Roman forces. In the year twenty-seven, there were conquests in the regions of the Maghreb. In the year twenty-eight, there was a second conquest of the western provinces. During this same period, a disagreement arose regarding the text of the Word of God — it was written down and in Ramadan, as is recorded and mentioned on various tongues, it was compiled. In the year twenty-nine, variant readings were burned. In the year thirty-three, armies from Khurasan advanced toward the city of Zaranj and recovered it. Then there was the matter of Uthman ibn Affan. In the year thirty-one, there was a conquest of Yemen. In the year thirty-two, there were events in certain cities, and the passing of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf al-Anzami, and Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet. And Abu Dihya — they held the Kaaba in great honor. And in the year thirty-three, there were raids, and the victors prevailed.

Uthman ibn Affan was [caliph], and the Jews' army was roused against Abdullah, in the origin. In the year thirty-five, there was an uprising against Uthman, and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, calmed it. The people returned to Egypt, and Marwan fortified the house against Uthman. In the month of Dhu al-Hijja, Uthman was killed by the rebels — those who had gone astray — and they were enemies of the religion of Islam. [His caliphate] lasted twelve years, and the caliphate [of Ali] began in the year thirty-six. In Jumada al-Awwal, the Battle of the Camel took place at Basra, between the Commander of the Faithful [Ali] and Aisha, Talha, and Zubayr. More than ten thousand men were killed in that battle. In that same year, at Siffin, the wife of the Prophet from Khaybar died; she passed away in Dhu al-Qi'da. In the year one hundred [and] forty, the arbitration [tahkim] took place between the Commander of the Faithful Ali and Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan — may the fire be upon him — through the tricks of Amr ibn al-As, the accursed, and the two arbiters. The intensity of strife grew, and the trouble of the Kharijites began there. More than ninety thousand Muslim men were killed in that battle. In the year thirty-seven, the Battle of Nahrawan against the Kharijites took place. In the year thirty-eight, Maymuna bint al-Harith, wife of the Prophet, passed away. In the year thirty-nine, Muawiya seized control of Iraq and its provinces, and the regions of Arab Iraq. In the year forty, in the month of Ramadan, the Commander of the Faithful Ali was killed in Kufa. He had ruled for four years and nine months, governing with strength and authority. In Rabi al-Awwal of the year forty, the Commander of the Faithful Hasan assumed the caliphate — but he held it for only a few months — and with that, the thirty years of the caliphate of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs came to an end. Then the governance, rule, dominance, and authority of [Muawiya] began.

The Umayyads — the first of them was Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Harb ibn Umayya, and their rule lasted [a given period], and fourteen of them held power. In the year forty-four, Umm Habiba, daughter of Abi Sufyan, the wife of the Prophet of God, passed away. In the year forty-five, Talha came, and there was [mention of] Iskand, and [descriptions of] those who were miserly, distracted, and covetous. In the year forty-nine, the death of the Commander of the Faithful, Hasan, occurred. In the year fifty-one, the death of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, the seventh and last of the ten who were given glad tidings of Paradise, took place. In the year fifty-six, the death of Hujaina, daughter of Harith, wife of the Prophet of God, occurred. In the year fifty-seven, the death of Aisha, [wife of the Prophet], the virgin [of the household], took place; and in the year fifty-nine, the death of Umm Salama, daughter of [Asir] al-Makhzumiyya, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad, occurred — she was among those who lived in the time of the Prophet. The Prophet passed away, and in the year seventy-one, the gathering [of forces] around Muhammad, the Commander of the Faithful, Husayn, took place. There was the valley and the event of the people of [Bakr's lands] and the flight to the vicinity of Medina, and the followers [were slaughtered] by the order of Yazid ibn Muawiya. In the year seventy-something, Abu Ubayda al-Thaqafi mastered [the region] and sought to dominate the lands of Iraq and the Arabs, and he killed [many]. Imam Husayn ('Ali's [son]) had governance for three years and held power. In the year sixty-four, the governance of Abdullah ibn [al-Zubayr] began; he fought battles, and [his forces] besieged the Haram, and the Ka'ba's covering was burned by fire. Thereafter, Abdullah ibn [al-Zubayr] returned to Medina and took control of [Mecca] and the Hijaz and gained [authority] over Iraq and Khorasan, and for eight years held governance there. In the year sixty-five, in Egypt, Syria, and elsewhere, a plague spread and many perished. People came to [various regions], and in Iraq there appeared an uprising, and those who first sought [vengeance for] Imam Husayn came forward, and two men sought kingship, and in the year sixty-something [events continued].

The killing of Umar Sa'd, may God curse him, and Shimr Dhi al-Jawshan, may God curse him, and most of those who killed Imam Husayn, peace be upon him, was carried out by Mukhtar al-Thaqafi, who had gained control over the regions of Diyar Bakr and Iraq. After that the dynasty of Muhallab ibn Abi Sufra lasted for forty years, and Abu Awsr Adhladh was also present. In the year sixty-seven [AH], Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad, may God curse him, was killed by Mukhtar. In the aforementioned Ramadan, Mukhtar al-Thaqafi was killed in battle with Mus'ab and fell. Mus'ab took his place as ruler. In the year sixty-eight, the appearance of the Asbiyyan persecution occurred. In the year seventy, Mus'ab was killed in battle against Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. That king brought Marwan's forces to Basra, and in the year seventy-two, the war of Hajjaj ibn Yusuf against Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr took place, and in that year on account of this the treasury was depleted. In the year seventy-three, the Ka'ba was besieged, and this was the conclusion of Hajjaj's campaign and the end of Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. In the year seventy-five, Hajjaj ibn Yusuf ibn al-Malik obtained the governorship over Iran, and he left no disorder or mismanagement unaddressed, yet he tormented the people of Iran for twenty years. In the year seventy-six, gold and silver coins of seventeen thousand were struck in the Arab lands, bearing the name of the Messenger, and these were circulated throughout the Arab regions. Likewise in this kingdom the name Hadhlabi was established, and the images of the kings were depicted. In the year eighty-two, the revolt of Ibn Ash'ab occurred, and Hajjaj campaigned against him for two years, and thousands of Muslims were killed in the west. In the year eighty-five, Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Biji al-Farisi served as the administrator of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and Abu al-Fadl was among the notable figures. There are descriptions of the moon and of Sinaqat and related matters and other things of that sort.

These are the crafts of this science that accountants now practice. Qabiba ibn Muslim gained governorship of Khorasan and ruled there for ten years. In the year seventy-four, in the month of Dhu al-Hijja, the pure Imam, Imam Zayn al-Abidin, passed away. In the year seventy-five came the release of the Sultan on the day of al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf. In the year seventy-seven, the rule of the Barmakids began — Ja'far al-Barmaki, who came to Balkh — and for a time he was minister and trusted man, and his position endured. His associates for two years held the ministry, and the world was generous and generosity filled the world. In the year one hundred and something, the Abbasid dynasty quietly began to rise. In the year one hundred and one, the curse was lifted and the insults against the Commander of the Faithful and his household by 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Marwani were ended. In the year one hundred and three came the consolidation of the Muhammadan dynasty. In the year one hundred and five, Abu al-Bashr Ka'b ibn 'Umar al-Ansari passed away — he was among the last of the companions of the Prophet's household and had carried the Prophet's flag. In the year one hundred and fourteen, Ghaylan of Damascus was deprived of his position and his school of thought. In the year one hundred and twenty-five, an army came to the region of Alans and into Afkhan, causing great destruction, but the army of Islam went and subdued them, and many of those people also came into Islam. In the year one hundred and seventeen, in the month of Rajab, the pure Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, peace be upon him, passed away. In the year one hundred and twenty-one, Zayd ibn Imam Zayn al-Abidin rose up, but they killed him and his followers were scattered, and the women of the Shia of the Household of the Prophet were driven away. In the year one hundred and twenty-nine, the Abbasid dynasty appeared.

Khorasan

In Khurasan, a horse of Abu Muslim, the master of the mission (Da'wa), and in the year one hundred and thirty-two, in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, the Banu Abbas appeared in Iraq and the tongue of al-Saffah, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, and without seven caliphs they were, in Ard and twenty-four years they exercised the caliphate, and in that same year the decline of the Banu Umayyad dynasty came to pass in Iran. And in the year one hundred and thirty-seven, Abu Muslim, master of the mission, was killed. And in the year one hundred and thirty-nine, the Banu Umayyad dynasty remained in Andalusia, and the duration of that dynasty was two hundred and seventy-three years, under Abdullah ibn Mu'awiya ibn Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and from among them those who ruled — and in the year one hundred and forty-four, the son of Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baqir, peace be upon him, passed away in Medina at the hands of four Sunnis, and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq carried him on people's shoulders to Medina and buried him in the earth. The Isma'ilis, who are the Sevener Shi'a, do not consider him a Muslim, and from that time Ja'far al-Sadiq was alive and the imamate passed to Imam Musa al-Kazim. And in the year one hundred and forty-eight, the death of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq occurred in Medina. And in the year one hundred and fifty-one, Abu Hanifa al-Kufi died in Baghdad. And in the year one hundred and sixty-six, Salih al-Hakim of Banu Hashim appeared, who claimed to be God and became intoxicated. And in the year one hundred and seventy, Andalusia belonged to the Banu Fatima, meaning from Andalusia, and three hundred and ten years this dynasty lasted. Its leaders were Abdullah ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Murtada, and by their rule they ordered, and both of them had Ibn al-Muqaffa' and a group killed, who had attempted to produce a rival to the Quran among the people. And in the year one hundred and seventy-five, the shrine of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, was made manifest.

In the time of Harun al-Rashid, [certain events occurred] and in the year ninety [AH], Malik ibn Anas al-Asbahi died in Medina. And in the year one hundred and eighty-three, in the month of Safar, the pure Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him, passed away. And in the year one hundred and eighty-nine, the decline of the Barmakid dynasty occurred, which had lasted about fifty-five years, and their authority had been held by seven rulers. And in the year one hundred and ninety-nine, in the month of Shawwal, the pure Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, peace be upon him, passed away in Tus. And in the year two hundred and four, in the month of Rajab, al-Shafi'i died in Egypt. And [al-Ma'mun] commanded the translation of works on wisdom, mathematics, astronomy, Euclid, Indian sciences, philosophy, medicine, geomancy, history, and other subjects from Syriac and Greek into Arabic. And in the year two hundred and ten, in the month of Rajab, the pure Imam Muhammad al-Jawad, peace be upon him, passed away in Baghdad. And in the year two hundred and twenty-three, Babak the heretic was killed. And in the year two hundred and twenty-four, [a certain scholar] of the Tabari school became known. And in the year two hundred and thirty-two, Ahmad ibn Hanbal died in Baghdad. And in the year two hundred and thirty-four, the people of various religions were pressured and became subject to certain rulings, and most of those known by the name Ghiyar [distinctive markings] were in this period. And in the year two hundred and thirty-six, the shrine of Imam Husayn was destroyed, and the waters in that land were cut off so that nothing remained, yet the blessed tomb endured, and the reason for this is known as the miracle of the saints, and in the year...

Husayn and two hundred: the dynasty of al-Daji al-Hayy Husayn ibn Buzurg al-Bashawarī ruled the kingdom of Iraq-i Ajam and Mazandaran for thirty-seven years, and his brother ruled part of the kingdom. In the year two hundred and fifty-three, the dynasty of Ranwali, that is the Tahirids, the Dhu al-Yaminayn, came to power. The beginning of the rule of the Banu Layth ibn Saffar over most of Iran lasted five years, and three persons held power: over Abbadan, Sijistan, Qanf, and Sind, and Nagha, in the district of Mudhar. These are counted among the disciples of Najm al-Khalidi, known as the martyred ones; the Prophet, peace be upon him, is reported to have spoken of the kings of Khurasan and the prosperity of India among them. In the year two hundred and fifty-something, in the month of Rajab, the death of the Imam al-Maasum Ali al-Naqi occurred — peace be upon him. In the year two hundred and fifty-five, the first of the Barqi Alawi dynasty arose, and the uprising of the slaves against the lords, with the victory of Nasr. In the year two hundred and sixty, in the month of Rabi al-Awwal, the death of Imam Hasan al-Askari occurred, peace be upon him, at Samarra. In the year two hundred and sixty-seven, in the month of Ramadan, the Occultation of the Imam, the Infallible Muhammad ibn al-Hayy — may God preserve him — occurred at Samarra. In the year two hundred and eighty-seven, the rule of the Samanids replaced that of the Saffarid Layth in Iran, led by the noble Ismail ibn Ahmad ibn Asad ibn Saman, of the lineage of Bahram Chubin. They ruled for one hundred and thirty-two and a half years, and nine persons held power. In the year two hundred and eighty-eight, the first rule of the lords of Tabaristan began, and in the year two hundred and ninety-four, the Qum region came to prominence. In the year two hundred and ninety-something, the Fatimid Ismaili dynasty appeared in Egypt and the Maghreb. These are the Banu Fatima, and in the year three hundred and something, they prevailed over the Aghlabids and assumed the title of Caliphate, and through the strengthening of their state with the hadith attributed to Ali, they came to prominence.

When the sun rises from the west, here the city of David was, and it lasted twenty-three years. In the Caliphate, the lineage of these people was present, and the tongue of the Mahdi, Muhammad ibn al-Rajni ibn Abdallah ibn al-Taqi Qasim ibn al-Wafa Ahmad ibn al-Wasi Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Jafar al-Sadiq was present. Fourteen persons ruled, and in the year three hundred and ten, the Caliph al-Muqtadir was in power, and the vizier Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ali, known as Ibn Muqla, invented the art of calligraphy.

In the year three hundred and nineteen, the Mahdi, Abu Said Habbabi, and the Qarmatians fought a great battle at Mecca during the pilgrimage season, killing many people, and they carried off the Black Stone and caused destruction. In the year three hundred and ten, the Buyid dynasty, the House of Buwayh, began in Iran, under the name Imad al-Dawla, and Ali ibn Buwayh received the kingdom. For one hundred and twenty-six years they held power, and seven persons ruled over them.

And similarly, the rulers of Tabaristan obtained sovereignty, and for more than a hundred years they held authority, and seven persons ruled. In the year three hundred and ninety-nine, the Qarmatians returned the Black Stone, and thirty thousand dinars in gold were sent by Abu Kulam Muti the Caliph to the Buyids. In the year three hundred and fifty-three, a great sea creature emerged from the Sea of Oman near Qabchalia and settled near the shore, appearing twice in the east.

Three times the eloquent one of the age spoke and said: "The time has drawn near," and Najm al-Amidi also spoke of this. In this same year, a virtuous man died in Medina, and a certain ruler came to his tomb and paid his respects. And in this same year, a group of Seljuks came from Turkestan and arrived in the land, and so it continued.

(Marginal note: Four hundred and some)

Ninety and three hundred: The fall of the Samanid dynasty and the beginning of the Ghaznavid state and sultanate — it began with Sabuktigin, and they remained in that state for one hundred and fifty years, and fourteen persons ruled. In the year three hundred and ninety, the uprising of the Banu Kilab began in the region of Syria, and around the year three hundred and ninety the idol-houses of Hindustan were [conquered] by Sultan Mahmud Ghazi, and he took away many idols of gold and silver by the thousands, distributing the plunder among the people.

In the year four hundred and nine, other regions of India also came under the rule of the Sultan Ghazi. In the year four hundred and ten, the Fatimid governor struck [blows] in Medina, and they dug tunnels up to [the graves of] Abu Bakr and Umar to bring them out. In those days, changes in the air and thunderbolts occurred in Medina, and great signs appeared, so that the people of Medina became frightened and came to the tomb of the Prophet, crying out, until the matter became known. They brought a veil [over the graves] and the Exalted Presence [of the Prophet's tomb] stopped those signs.

In the year four hundred and sixteen, the Seljuks came from beyond and arrived with their multitude. In the year four hundred and twenty, Sheikh al-Ra'is Abu Ali Sina (Avicenna) established the method of accounting, and from him came better reckonings and contents such as the Frankish [formulas], and they were freed. In the year four hundred and twenty-four, the Fatimid [dynasty] fell in some parts of Andalusia.

In the year four hundred and twenty-nine, the Seljuk state arose; their first [ruler] was Tughril Bek, son of Mika'il, son of Seljuq. They held sovereignty over central Iran for one hundred and sixty-some years, and several persons ruled. In the year four hundred and thirty-three, the first ruling Qadir among the Seljuqs was Bughra Khan; they ruled for one hundred and fifty years and fifteen persons ruled.

In the year four hundred and forty-eight, the dynasty of the Al-i Buya fell, and in the year four hundred and fifty, the Ismailis of Egypt, through the agency of al-Basasiri of Mosul, advanced into Iraq and imprisoned the Caliph al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah, ruling for one year and four months. In the year four hundred and sixty-four, on account of a dispute with the vizier Nizam al-Mulk Hasan, registers and account books were drawn up. In the eighties, arms were gathered in Rum, and Dawud ibn Sulayman ibn Qutalmish ibn Saljuq Shah ruled there for twenty years, and fourteen persons held the sultanate from among the commanders. In the same year the Fatimid dynasty continued in some parts of Andalus, and in the year four hundred and eighty-one, the Atabegs of Diyarbakr arose, among them the Salghurids from the direction of the Seljuk Sultan Malikshah, and they remained in power for approximately one hundred and eighty-two years as atabegs, exercising authority. In that same year, others proclaimed themselves kings, and the rulers of Mardin still hold power. In the year four hundred and eighty-three, Hasan Sabbah ascended to the fortress of Alamut and founded the state of the Ismailis in the upper regions of Tabaristan; for one hundred and eighty-some years they propagated their doctrine in excess, and eight persons exercised rule. In the year four hundred and ninety, the Franks seized Jerusalem from the Muslims, killing more than seven thousand Muslims and bringing ruin. The foundation of the Khwarazmshah dynasty was laid there — their glory and dignity — Qutb al-Din Muhammad ibn Tukhtakeen served as governor and then as king for approximately one hundred and some years. In the year five hundred and five, the Qumari forces reached the mountain fortresses of Ismaili Syria. Iran and that region sought to bring the Arab community, and in the year...

Four hundred and five fortresses — the fortress of Abd al-Malik Attash and the battle of Isfahan belonged to him, and the castles of those people were seized by the Seljuk-loving Sultan, and the most notable of them were recorded in the register of the army. And in the Khorasan madrasa the Sultan's decree was issued, and the idol-worshippers were driven out from Babarum. Every year they sent men to strengthen the religion of Islam and humiliate them in such a manner. And in the year four hundred and twenty-five, the rule and kingship of the Qara-Khitai began, in Balasaghun and Arbrowan, and they ruled over a hundred and two regions. The kings of Lakhnaur Muhammad and their vassals issued decrees, and in the year five hundred and thirty-some, the battle of the Muslims with the Qara-Khitai took place at the plain of Qatwān, and the Islamic forces were defeated. And in the year five hundred and forty-three, the Atabegs of Fars — the Salghurids — first arose, their foremost being Sunqur ibn Mawdud. From the lineage of Ushturān, Sunqur of Nakhcheh-Taq, son of A'wan Zakhān, they held power for one hundred and twenty years, and eleven atabegs exercised authority. And in the year five hundred and forty-five, the Ghaznavid state ended and the rule of the Ghurid sultans began, starting with Ala al-Dawla Walr Hasan ibn Husayn ibn Sam, of the lineage of the Suri kings, the rulers of Ghur. Their kings were five in number, and their sultanate lasted four years altogether. And in the year five hundred and forty-eight, the event of Ghazna occurred at its end. And in the year five hundred and forty-nine, Genghis Khan was born, in the time of the Caliph al-Muqtafi and Sanjar and Bozmilik Shah the Seljuk. And in the year five hundred and fifty, the rule of the Atabegs of Lor began; their first was Abu Tahir ibn Muhammad Ali ibn Abi al-Husayn al-Fadlawi, and they have ruled approximately one hundred and ninety years; among their rulers one named Nargis Atabeg is mentioned. And in the year five hundred and fifty-six...

The Ismaili state was in Egypt and the Maghreb, and the beginning of the rule of the house of Abu Bakr — the first of them was King Salah al-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub, master of the Khass and his family. They remained in that state for nearly one hundred years, and some four hundred rulers governed. In the year five hundred and fifty-nine, the proclamation of the doctrine of permissiveness appeared by the king of the Ismailis, Burlunsabhi — that is, Kiya Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Buzurg-Ummid of Rudbar, whom the people of Alamut called upon and regarded as their summoner. They claimed he was descended from Nizar ibn Fatimi of the Maghreb, and he entirely abolished the commands and prohibitions of religious law, calling that day the Day of Resurrection, and they abandoned the old calendar and replaced it with a new one. In the year five hundred and sixty-one, Abu Bakr took Syria away from those who held it — Sayf al-Din Ghazi ibn Mawdud ibn Tekish ibn Aq Sunqur — and from that time it has remained with Egypt. In the year five hundred and eighty, the state of Qutlugh Atabakan of Luristan arose, and their leading figure was Husam al-Din Khurshid; for one hundred and fifty years fifteen rulers governed them. In the year five hundred and eighty-one, in the month of Rajab, seven planets aligned in the third degree of Libra and met together, all in the airy triplicity — a grand conjunction of all the planets — and the astrologers ruled that at the time of this conjunction a quarter of the inhabited world would be destroyed by flood and wind, like mountains that the wind tears down, and hollows would be carved into the earth. Those who took shelter from the flood and wind survived. When the time of morning came and the season of autumn rains approached, the doors were opened, but the grain of that year was not cleansed of insects by the wind. Two orders were issued to light lamps atop minarets so that the wind would extinguish them, and this seemed fitting.

And although the tradition of the honored Prophet affirms the truth, no revelation came down upon Muhammad from on high concerning this. One who is close [to this meaning] has said: "You were a light, so that because of ill winds the mountain fortresses would be ruined and plundered; on the day of judgment, let it be as the wind. O sender of the winds, you know and illuminate." In the year three hundred and eighty-something, Harun brought Jerusalem [Bayt al-Maqdis] under control through Farrukhmiyan and carried out a great slaughter. In the year two hundred and sixty-something, the power of the Seljuqs in Iran came to an end and the rule of the Khwarazmian kings over Iraq-i Ajam began. In the year sixty-eight and two hundred, the state of Genghis Khan appeared — a great king known by the title of Padishah — and he became a great sovereign. In the year ninety-something and two hundred, the power of the 'Awur [Gur Khan] came to an end and the rule of the sipahsalars of Georgia over their people began, and it lasted for approximately seventy-something years. In the year twenty-something and two hundred, the state of the Qara-Khitai came to an end. The king's daughter was given in marriage to the Khan of Nayiman, and the Sultan of Khwarazm [took power]. In the same year, Genghis Khan made a pact and agreement with the Sultan of Khwarazm and conquered Bukhara. In the year six hundred and thirteen, he reached Jurjan; Genghis Khan had Iran's princes killed, since the Shah of Khwarazm had plotted against him with ill advice. In the year six hundred and twenty-something, [Genghis Khan] arrived at Beijing [Khitai] and the remainder of Iran and Turan was subdued. In that year, events occurred in the regions of Kashghar, Khotan, and surrounding areas. In the year six hundred and sixteen, the lands of Transoxiana and Khurasan were [brought under his rule]. In the year six hundred and seventeen, the nations of Khurasan, Iraq-i Ajam, Adharbayjan, Iran, and those provinces were [devastated]. In the year six hundred and eighteen, he again brought other provinces of Iran under his control, and tens of thousands of people were killed without cause, and the world was laid to ruin.

Whoever was complete among them, and if a thousand more were sent, calamity would befall them and that advantage would not be maintained.
Reason: The Turkish composite was weak in its foundation, and its support fell away from its hands.
Like a cypress whose feet and base are without roots and without strength, from affection it diminishes and from hatred it breaks.
In the year 621, the first era of the dynasty of the Seljuks fell, and their commander Baraq Hajib ibn Borbajtan, one of the amirs of Gur Khan, and eighty years their rule lasted, and Mongols became their rulers, and in the year 628 came the fall of the dynasty of the Khwarazmian Shahs, and the Mongol amirs took them and ruled for seventy-odd years, and four names of command came to pass. And in the year 653 came the fall of the Ismaili power in Iran and the conquest of their fortresses by Hulagu Khan, son of Ölü Khan, son of Genghis Khan, who came to Iran. And in the year 654 came the fall of the Abbasid Caliphs of Iran, and Hulagu Khan settled there. And in the year 660 came the fall of the dynasty of the rulers of Diyarbakir by Hulagu Khan, in the year 661 the departure of Rani Sa—, and afterwards Bukhara and its fortress were taken by al-Maju, and in the year 675 appeared strife and turbulence and calamities and the conquest of the Crimea and its rulers by the Mongol army. And in the year 694, Ghazan Khan embraced Islam, and with him many peoples of Iran became Muslim — may God have mercy on the martyred — and Al-Ghazi spread the message and the churches and temples throughout Iran were all converted. And from the lineage of Luqay Khan ibn Genghis Khan, most became Muslim, and the greater part of the Mongol peoples there became Muslim, and the kings became [Muslim].

In the regions of Cathay, Khotan, and Machin, in subsequent years, the Qa'an descended from the line of Qubilai Khan son of Tolui Khan son of Chinggis Khan converted to Islam, and from his line came those who embraced Islam. With this development, among the Turkic rulers, one from the line of Chagatai Khan son of Chinggis Khan also converted to Islam, and the people likewise turned to the faith. In all four ulus the practice of Islam spread and flourished, and the meaning holds that "precedence belongs to the one who came first."

As for the state of Ghazan Khan: in the year 699 came the fall of the state of Rum, and in the year 706 came the fall of the Qara-Khitai sultans of Kirman, and in the year 716 the name of the Companions was removed from the Friday sermon because Sultan Muhammad Khudabanda — may God have mercy on him — ordered it so.

In the year 740, which is five years since Iran's capital came under tribulation, following the death of the blessed king Abu Sa'id — may God illuminate him — amid the strife of the Ilkhanate, trouble and chaos ensued, because those who had been raised up by the state, each of them now holds power, and the pillars of the kingdom each pursue their own opinion, with no other course available. Having turned away from the kingdom, each seeks his own benefit, and the refuge of the people is gone. The people of the world have abandoned their goods and possessions, and the craftsmen and inhabitants of the cities find no place of security, nor do masters and servants have any settled abode. The people of Iran have been driven to despair by the oppression of rulers, and the entire population of the world is deprived of security and safety. The governance of the country has reached a state where its form is only nominal. Kings emerge from the provinces in rebellion, and in the course of seven kings within the realm, many have been slain and left in the central lands of Iran, while on the outskirts and in the provinces conquest prevails, and now throughout the realm, the people seek a sovereign worthy of rule.

Among the princes and amirs of Bab-chan, Iran, and Georgia: Suleiman Khan Panbara, the son of Shehrzad, was appointed by Hulagu Khan as ruler, and Amir Shaikh Hasan Jalad; and among the amirs of Diyar Bakr and Baghdad: Jahanpur Khan, son of Lafur Siyak ibn Kunjukhan, was installed as king; and the amirs of Khurasan: Tugha Banu Khan ibn Hajji Khan was named king; and likewise Sadd Talab ibn Malik al-Azal.

In Naga-buy, Ata az the Oppressor ruled over the region, and all those within his ranks — if their great opposition became known, they would resist and fight. Armies and subjects came and went, levying tribute and passing through, and security was lost. Affairs changed all around.

For the most part, the Friday sermon (khutba) was read in the name of Takji, another sovereign, and the coin (sikka) was struck in the name of Hamah Razd, and the khutba was read in the name of Minal Lanat and Bayjam by force — these matters are recorded.

But by the grace of God, things came right again, security was restored, and the world became orderly.

Verse: The just sovereign arose / So that justice and rectitude might return / Like pure water flowing clean / Bringing prosperity and order.

As for the governors of the western regions of Iran who held authority: among them was Malik Bahjam al-Din Mas'ud al-Muzaffar, who governed Fars, Kirman, and the surrounding districts; and Jalal al-Din Mas'ud Shah was made supreme in Iran; Mahmud Shah was given Sistan and Hormuz and the surrounding islands; Qutb al-Din governed Lar and its dependencies; Jalal al-Din Iqrasiyab was amir of Nazlim; Ahmad Krasnal was restored to Sind and its districts; and the amir of Herat was appointed. Malik ibn Ghaniyan al-Din Kart, and among the amirs of Gilan and the other kings and amirs of Gilan.

And from the account of this art, from Sabar of Zanjan and Barazaranajam remaining in the same way, these rulers govern by religion in their current affairs, but no community has escaped these troubles and hardships without the peace of the realm, for the realm is ruined by wandering, and the king does not remedy it, and the wretched subjects do not submit to these decrees, and because of this, the subjects cannot advance in obedience to the king's army — this is called [a certain term].

It is said in this state: "Give thanks to God, this community is enriched; show kindness to the poor and destitute in this matter; may the absent ones be guided." And God knows best. The lords and kings have wisely established among the people of Qara: the sons of Qublan Khan, son of Wali Khan, son of Chinggis Khan; and among the Turkic peoples, Shirin Khan son of Chagatai Khan son of Chinggis Khan; and in the Ulus of the Qipchaq steppe, from the lineage of the Ulus of Chagatai, Özbeg Khan son of Tawahmir Khan son of Nöqö Qa'an son of Anö Khan son of Chinggis Khan are the rulers. And it is remarkable that previously, despite the authority of the kings of these lands, they sought to overcome them, and their armies most often turned to the worst direction. Now in such a solitude, this community's intercessor is absent. And it is clear that the world is wide, the glory of the world, and its power is maintained by the art and strength of the monarch and the multitude and the few of the army.

O God, Lord of dominion, You grant sovereignty and take sovereignty from whom You will. The proof of this matter is clear, and among the kings who have seized Hindustan, Sultan Alauddin, the ruler of the realm, was generous and of high rank, and from his station the community stood and remained among the nations.

The Sultan holds governance and rule, and among the Arabs the Bedouin Ibn Isa holds the emirate, and among the peoples of Egypt and Syria Multa Nasir al-Din Qalladan is king of forty and of paradise, and among the peoples of Lesser Armenia Bakfur is king, and in those lands there are also disputes arising among the women causing turmoil and strife. May God the Most High, Glorified and Exalted, look with mercy and compassion upon them, and He has bestowed upon all the cities safety and complete security, spreading justice and order. May God enhance his glory and his generosity and grace. This solar calendar is counted thus and it is so, because in every fourth year they add a fourth day to Shebat, and they add it to twenty, and in other years it remains at twenty-eight. The names of their months and their numbers and their signs are as follows: 1. Tishri I, 2. Tishri II, 3. Kanun I, 4. Kanun II, 5. Shebat, 6. Adar, 7. Nisan, 8. Iyar, 9. Haziran I, 10. Haziran II, 11. Ab, 12. Elul.
This calendar was attributed by those of his era to Alexander, and from that it became known as the Alexandrian calendar, and among its months Iyar is the most famous. The Christians claim that on the twenty-fifth of Kanun I, Jesus, peace be upon him, was born in the region of Nazareth near Hebron, in the district called al-Muqaddam, and the Christians call those who deny this the misguided. And that year corresponds to three hundred and thirty-eight years of the Alexandrian era, corresponding to the year sixty-eight and seventy of the Coptic reckoning. And on the last Saturday of Kanun I, Zechariah and Jesus son of Mary performed the rite of baptism — that is, immersion — and the Holy Spirit descended upon Jesus, and the Christians celebrate that day. And from the twelfth to the last of Kanun II it concludes and Saturday comes.

First

The first is the fast of Asmo, which lasts three days and a little more than three weeks — that is to say their fast lasts seven weeks, which amounts to forty-seven days, because the last Saturday falls [in this period] and their Feast of Breaking the Fast most often coincides with the middle days between Nisan. Whatever falls between the last Saturday and Sunday should be fasted, and in the last seven weeks they have weighty answers, and they wished to witness the last Sunday of this fast with their own eyes. It is said that on this day Jesus, peace be upon him, came riding humbly into Jerusalem, and he called people to the faith, and [illegible] called the Jews to faith in him, and they bore him a grudge. On Friday the chief of the Jews came, and one who resembled Jesus in appearance was crucified in his place — they sought the prayer of absolution. Then on Saturday after that they sought to kill him, and on Wednesday, the fortieth day, was their Feast of Breaking the Fast. They sought to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, but on that day he ascended to heaven. On the fifth day of their feast, which was Saturday, they sought intercession, and it is said that on that day the Holy Spirit descended upon the prophets and the mission of Jesus, peace be upon him, was proclaimed. In the writings of Abu Rayhan it is recorded that the Christians say their prophet lived among them and two companions, a male and female, would go out together in a gathering, and whatever man had a wife, he should cohabit with her properly — this is the correct account. As for the Mondays, the act is forbidden, and for Jesus on other Mondays likewise this act is forbidden for the appointed number. Always on the eighteenth of Adhar the sun reaches its first point and arrives at its exaltation; and on the nineteenth of Rajab the sun reaches [its station] and the rising of Sirius in the south occurs, and the duration of [its period] continues.

The people of Buna: it appears in the middle of this week, and both are from the fine fish of the heart, as described. The beginning of summer is well-known for its clarity, abundance, and plenty of water. The sun is in the fifth degree of Virgo, and the form of heat diminishes, and the temperament of the air changes. The Arabs in the season of heat have said in verse: "When I am separated from the water for twenty years, we feel the cold from every direction." In the eighth month, Sirius rises at the position of Fanab, and it is dry and thirsty. The degree is Aquarius, and the first Jumra belongs to the Jumrat al-Ma, known until that time. With it the eighth Sinbat Jumra, the second, belongs, and they call it Jumrat al-Nar, meaning: whenever the earth's fire comes down, and in the low and less regions the third Jumra exists. They call it Jumrat al-Ikhtiyar, meaning the trees grow by the grace of God, because the air of the equator causes heat in the hot regions from this smoke daily. In the period of Sinbat, the first cold of al-Ajuz has come — it is said that the people of Ad were destroyed by it, and nothing remained of them except ruins. They say this to their people, the people of Kurd, calling it: the Arabs call it the weakness of the year; it returns when the cold has settled and the warmth comes after it. It appears that the cold of al-Ajuz lasts a week, and every people counts eight days and seven nights. And the speech of Jumayda from the number of the descriptions of seven nights and eight days of continuous cold; and the cold of al-Ajuz is read by some scholars; and it is attributed to Yaqub al-Kindi among the non-Arabs, and others determine the calendar of the days from when the sun reaches its apogee by degrees. And now the count of the treatises from this date is six hundred and some and one year, which is 115[6]. The Turkic names: al-Ghawran, and the Turks also call it Qarist, and the first night is Khaltan-Ol.
